title: The heart as a lump of flesh
word: The heart as a lump of flesh
hookLine: there is a lump of flesh in the body: if it is sound, all is sound. it is the heart (Bukhari)

cards: Put a hand flat on the left side of your chest. Under it, a muscle is doing its work without being asked. The Prophet ﷺ pointed at something like it in a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, narrated by al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.
Truly, in the body there is a lump of flesh. If it is sound, the whole body is sound. If it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt.
Truly, it is the heart. One small piece of the body, and everything else follows it.

teach.h: QALB: A SMALL PIECE OF FLESH.
teach.b: The heart in Arabic is qalb, and in the hadith it's called a mudghah, a small piece of flesh. That's the surprise: the thing everything depends on is small, plain and easy to overlook.

Muslim teachers read it as pointing through the organ that pumps blood to the inner center of a person, the place where intentions are made. Yesterday's ikhlas lives there, and so does every station from these two weeks.
Another hadith, in Sahih Muslim, says Allah does not look at your bodies or your appearance, but looks at your hearts and your deeds. And the Qur'an names what will help on the last day.
In Pickthall's translation, it is the day when wealth and sons avail not, "Save him who bringeth unto Allah a whole heart."
A whole heart, a sound one, qalb salim. That word sound is the hinge.
Hearts can be healthy, and hearts can get sick. This new part of the path takes the sicknesses one at a time, arrogance, envy and others, the way a doctor would.
First, look back at this week: gratitude with the whole self, the tied camel, contentment even through tears, love that follows, fear and hope as two wings, sincerity. All of it was heart-work.
And the Prophet ﷺ is reported to have asked Allah, the Turner of hearts, to make his heart firm. Even he asked for his heart to be kept.

how: Muslims learn this hadith as a teaching that the heart, the inner center of a person, governs everything else, and teachers of the inward path speak of keeping the heart sound and treating its diseases.

games.q: what does “the heart as a lump of flesh” mean?
o: a muscle that grows stronger with every single prayer
the heart: a small piece of flesh the whole body follows
the stomach, which must be kept from eating too much

s: the hadith is only about the organ that pumps blood
Muslim teachers read it as pointing through the organ to the inner center of a person, where intentions are made.
a hadith in Sahih Muslim says Allah looks at hearts and deeds, not bodies and appearance
not your bodies or your appearance, but your hearts and your deeds.
in the Qur'an, wealth and sons help on the last day
they avail not, "save him who bringeth unto Allah a whole heart."

games.q: the Prophet ﷺ says there is one piece of flesh in the body that everything else follows. which is it?
games.why: if it is sound, the whole body is sound; if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. truly, it is the heart.

practice: Rest your palm flat on your chest and feel the beat, steady, asking nothing from you: this small thing is keeping you alive right now.
Then ask gently how the other heart is today, the one the hadith points through, and name it in one word, heavy, light, busy, tight, calm, with no fixing.
If you pray, recall the Prophet's words, O Turner of hearts; if not, keep your hand where it is and breathe.

wordCard.voice: The heart as a lump of flesh. The qalb: a small piece of the body that everything follows; when it is sound, all of you is sound. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a small piece of flesh, a morsel: the hadith's word for the heart.
